code.description: The Connect code, like not_found or invalid_argument.

machine.v1.CommandCost.description: CommandCost is what a command of a project costs, over the runs Djinn measured. The peak memory is the resident memory of the command's largest process, children included once they ended; 0 where the system does not give it (Windows).

command.description: The command and its arguments, as run, up to 200 characters; case is ignored.

cpuSeconds.description: Mean CPU time of a run, user and system, in seconds: the command and the children it waited for.

lastCpuSeconds.description: CPU time of the last run, in seconds.

lastExitCode.description: Exit code of the last run.

lastPeakMemoryBytes.description: Peak memory of the last run, in bytes.

lastSeconds.description: Duration of the last run, in seconds.

peakMemoryBytes.description: Highest peak memory of a run, in bytes.

seconds.description: Mean duration of a run, in seconds.

project.description: Only the commands of this project, by name or identifier.

costs.description: The commands, by project, the most run first.

machine.v1.Gate.description: Gate is a gate held or waited for.

holder.description: Who holds it, and what for; empty when nobody does.

holderTaskId.description: Task of the holder; empty for a holder outside any task.

name.description: Name of the gate, in lower case.

waiting.description: Who waits for it, the next one first.

gates.description: The gates held or waited for.

machine.v1.Machine.description: Machine is the machine Djinn runs on, as read now.

cpuPressure.description: CPU pressure; absent where the system gives none (Linux without PSI, macOS, Windows).

load1.description: Load average over the last minute; absent where the system gives none (Windows).

memoryAvailableBytes.description: Memory available to new programs, in bytes.

memoryPressure.description: Memory pressure; absent where the system gives none.

pressure.description: Why the machine is under pressure; empty when it is not. Under pressure, no worker starts and no gate is granted.

workers.description: The most workers Djinn runs at once on this machine.

machine.v1.Pressure.description: Pressure is how much of the time tasks of the machine waited for a resource: the pressure stall information of Linux.

fullAvg10.description: Percent of the last 10 seconds during which every task waited.

someAvg10.description: Percent of the last 10 seconds during which at least one task waited.

plan.v1.Allowance.description: Allowance is a right the developer allows a wish's workers in one of its projects, an explicit decision that applies to every task of the wish in that project, and to no other wish.

note.description: Free text that comes with the choice.

plan.v1.Block.description: A block is free content of a wish, laid out by the lead: a decision taken outside a question, a section of analysis, a line of the journal, a diagram. Djinn computes nothing from it, and shows a kind it does not know as text: nothing is lost.

kind.description: What the block is, in a word the lead chooses: decision, section, log, diagram, report…

marks.description: What the developer marked on it from the window: read, approved.

mediaType.description: Media type of the content: text/markdown when empty, or another, like application/json.

position.description: Order within the wish, lowest first. New blocks go 1000 after the last one, so that a block slips between two others without moving them.

taskId.description: Task the block is about, if any.

kind.description: Only the blocks of this kind, case ignored.

taskId.description: Only the blocks about this task.

content.description: The content, Markdown unless --media-type says otherwise.

id.description: The block to change; a new block when empty.

kind.description: What the block is, in a word: decision, section, log, diagram, report…

mediaType.description: Media type of the content, like application/json; text/markdown by default.

position.description: Order within the wish; by default 1000 after the last block, for a new one.

plan.v1.Choice.description: Choice is an answer to a question: YES for a question without options, or the letter of an option.

plan.v1.Lead.description: The lead of a wish: an agent session the user talks to, in the lead's terminal. Never a secret: the provider and the session's identifier, which the agent's own command line resumes.

directory.description: Folder the session runs in on this machine: an agent finds its sessions by folder. An export replaces it by its project's name or ~, and an import puts this machine's folder back when it knows it.

provider.description: Kind of agent: claude or codex.

sessionId.description: Identifier of the session, as the agent names it: claude --resume takes it.

plan.v1.Mark.description: A mark the developer puts on a question, a decision or a block: read, or approved as it is. The lead reads the marks in the wish's brief and with djinn mark list.

remove.description: Take the mark off instead. An answer stays.

target.description: What to mark: a question's code, like Q03, or the identifier of a question or of a block.

wishId.description: Wish of the question, needed only when its code exists in several wishes.

marked.description: The mark, and what it is on.

plan.v1.MarkTarget.description: MarkTarget points to what a mark is on: a question by its code, or a question or a block by its identifier. Set one of: code, id.

id.description: The identifier of a question or of a block.

plan.v1.Marked.description: Marked is a mark with what it is on.

blockId.description: The block marked, if it is one.

label.description: The question's code, or the block's kind.

questionId.description: The question marked, if it is one.

title.description: The question's text, or the block's title, in a line.

wishId.description: Wish of the question or block.

plan.v1.Project.description: A project is a folder Djinn works in, a Git repository or not.

directory.description: Absolute path of the folder on this machine, symbolic links resolved. Empty for a project an imported wish names but this machine does not have yet: djinn project add <folder> attaches it.

git.description: Whether the folder is inside a Git repository.

name.description: Short name, unique without regard to case.

remote.description: URL of the Git remote, origin or else the first one, without credentials; empty without one. Another machine finds the project by it, case ignored.

summons.description: Skills of other projects this project summons: its workers get them at launch, nothing is copied.

plan.v1.ProjectAllowance.description: ProjectAllowance is the right a wish allows its workers in one project.

plan.v1.ProjectMatch.description: ProjectMatch is how one project of an imported wish was found on this machine.

note.description: What to check or do, when there is something.

plan.v1.ProjectMatchKind.description: ProjectMatchKind says how an imported project was found on this machine.

directory.description: The folder of the project; a relative path starts from the current directory.

name.description: Short name, unique without regard to case; by default the name of the folder.

plan.v1.Provider.description: Provider is the kind of agent a worker runs.

plan.v1.Question.description: A question an agent asks the developer. Once answered, it is a decision.

answer.description: The answer; a question that has one is a decision.

code.description: Short code to dictate, like Q03, unique within the wish and never reused.

context.description: What is at stake, in Markdown: what the answer changes, what each option costs.

marks.description: What the developer marked on it from the window: read, approved.

options.description: Options offered, answered by their letter: A for the first one, then B, C and D.

recommendation.description: The option the asker recommends, and why, in Markdown. Starting with its letter (B: …) lets the developer approve it in one click.

revision.description: How many times the lead revised it.

rounds.description: Its rounds, oldest first: each request to investigate, each revision by the lead. The last one an open question has is a request: it is being investigated, and waits for the lead, not for the developer.

plan.v1.QuestionRef.description: QuestionRef points to a question by its code or by its identifier. Set one of: code, id.

choice.description: The choice: yes, or the letter of an option. On options that say yes and no, yes or no, in any language Djinn speaks.

note.description: Why this choice, or what to do with it.

question.description: The question to answer: its code, like Q03, or its identifier.

wishId.description: Wish of the question, needed only when its code exists in several wishes.

context.description: What is at stake, in Markdown: what the answer changes, what each option costs.

options.description: An option the developer can pick; repeat for each one, up to four.

recommendation.description: The option you recommend, and why, in Markdown.

text.description: The question, in one or two sentences.

note.description: What to dig into before deciding.

question.description: The question: its code, like Q03, or its identifier.

wishId.description: Wish of the question, needed only when its code exists in several wishes.

open.description: Only the questions still waiting for an answer.

since.description: Only the questions asked at or after this time.

wishId.description: Only the questions of this wish.

context.description: What is at stake now, in Markdown; the former context when empty.

options.description: The options now, up to four; the former ones when none.

question.description: The question: its code, like Q03, or its identifier.

recommendation.description: The option you recommend now, and why; the former recommendation when empty.

wishId.description: Wish of the question, needed only when its code exists in several wishes.

plan.v1.Round.description: A round of a question before it is decided: a request to investigate, or the lead's revision.

context.description: For a revision, what the question said before it.

note.description: For a request, what to dig into.

options.description: For a revision, the options before it.

recommendation.description: For a revision, the recommendation before it.

plan.v1.Skill.description: A skill as a project sees it: its own, or summoned from another project.

description.description: What it does, from its SKILL.md.

directory.description: Its folder on this machine, in the project that holds it.

missing.description: Why a summoned skill cannot be found; empty when it is.

project.description: The project that uses the skill.

source.description: Where a summoned skill comes from, as <project>/<skill>; empty for the project's own.

project.description: Only the skills of this project, by name or identifier.

skills.description: The skills, by project then name.

into.description: The project that summons it, by name or identifier.

skill.description: The skill, as <project>/<skill>: the project that holds it, then its folder name. Case ignored.
The skill, as the project now sees it.

from.description: The project that summoned it, by name or identifier.

skill.description: The skill, as <project>/<skill>, as it was summoned. Case ignored.

plan.v1.Summon.description: A skill a project summons from another project. It stays in its source, and the summoning project follows it: Djinn shows each worker the source's folder as it is, by its agent's own path, and writes nothing in the project.

projectId.description: The project that holds the skill.

skill.description: The skill's folder name, in that project's .agents/skills or .claude/skills.

plan.v1.Task.description: A task is one item of a wish's flight plan, done in one project.

access.description: Where its worker's rights come from.

code.description: Short code to dictate, like W2, unique within the wish.

dependsOn.description: Tasks that must be done before this one starts, by identifier. A task whose dependency ends without being done fails too.

editQuestionId.description: The question asking the developer whether the worker may edit the project's files, for a task whose access is, or was, ASKING.

error.description: Why the task failed or stopped.

exitCode.description: Exit code of the worker's process, once it ended.

forkOf.description: Where the fork comes from, for a reader: the code of the task (W1), or "lead".

forkSession.description: The session the worker started from, forked: a copy of another task's or of the lead's conversation, with a new session of its own. Empty for a worker that starts from its prompt alone, the default. Stays on this machine: an export leaves it out.

maxBudgetUsd.description: Most the task may spend, in US dollars, over all its runs; 0 for no cap.

model.description: Model of the agent, as spawned; empty for the provider's default. A worker started again keeps it.

projectId.description: Project the task works in; empty for a task outside any project, which only reads.

provider.description: Kind of agent that works on the task.

scheduled.description: Djinn starts the task's worker by itself, once its dependencies are done, its scopes free and a slot free: the task was spawned or planned on this machine. A task imported with a wish is not.

sessionId.description: Session of the agent, to resume it.

usage.description: What the worker spent so far, summed over its runs.

waitReason.description: Why a planned task has not started yet; empty once it has.

worktree.description: Root of the task's Git worktree, in Djinn's data folder; empty outside Git, where the worker runs in the project folder.

writeScopes.description: What the task writes, as paths in the project's folder ("src", "docs/api.md"); empty for the whole folder. Outside Git, two tasks whose scopes overlap never run together. In Git, each task has its own worktree, and scopes are not checked.

plan.v1.TaskAccess.description: TaskAccess says where the rights of a task's worker come from (docs/providers.md, "What a worker may do").

plan.v1.TaskEvent.description: An event of a task's worker: what it said, the tools it called, what it spent.

raw.description: The provider's line as it came, when the event comes from one.

seq.description: Position in the task, from 1, with no gap.

text.description: The event for a reader: the text, the tool and its input, the error.

usage.description: What the worker spent so far, on a usage event.

plan.v1.TaskEventKind.description: TaskEventKind says what a worker event is. Its content stays free text.

force.description: Remove the worktree even when it holds changes not committed.

projectId.description: Only the tasks in this project.

wishId.description: Only the tasks of this wish.

text.description: The message, as the worker reads it.

event.description: The message, as an event of the task.

dependsOn.description: A task of the same wish that must be done first: its code (W1) or its identifier.

fork.description: Start the worker from a copy of this task's conversation (its code, W1, or its identifier), with a session of its own, instead of from the prompt alone. The inherited context is read again at every turn: prefer a short prompt, the default. Claude and Codex fork; Antigravity cannot.

fromLead.description: Start the worker from a copy of the lead's conversation, as --fork does from a task.

later.description: Only plan the task: the call returns at once, and djinn up starts the worker when the task is ready.

maxBudgetUsd.description: Most the worker may spend, in US dollars, when the provider can enforce it.

model.description: Model of the agent; by default the provider's.

projectId.description: Project to work in; by default the wish's project, when it has only one. For a wish without any project, the task runs outside any project: read-only, in an empty folder of its own.

prompt.description: What to ask the worker; by default the title.

provider.description: Kind of agent; by default claude.

title.description: What the task does, in a sentence.

writeScopes.description: A path the task writes, in the project's folder; none for the whole folder. Outside Git, tasks whose scopes overlap never run together.

task.description: The task: running, or waiting with its reason.

plan.v1.TaskStatus.description: TaskStatus is where a task stands.

plan.v1.Usage.description: Usage is what a worker spent, as its provider reports it.

cacheReadTokens.description: Tokens read from the prompt cache.

cacheWriteTokens.description: Tokens written to the prompt cache.

costUsd.description: Cost in US dollars, as the provider computes it.

plan.v1.Wish.description: A wish is what you ask Djinn for, and what it works to grant. It may span several projects.

allowances.description: Rights the developer allows the wish's workers, per project, ahead of any task.

grantTime.description: When the user granted the wish.

lead.description: The lead: the agent session that drives the wish, for djinn wish resume to take it back.

rank.description: Place among the active wishes, from 1: the first one has priority. 0 for a paused or granted wish.

ready.description: Djinn proposes to grant the wish: it has tasks, all finished, no question is open, and no task waits for an answer or failed. Computed on every read, never stored. Only the user grants a wish.

state.description: Where the wish stands: active, paused or granted. Three wishes are active at most.

title.description: What is wished, in a sentence.

mode.description: The right: edit, auto, or none to take it back.

projectId.description: The project; by default the wish's project, when it has only one.

text.description: The brief, in Markdown: the stable part, then the part that moves.

file.description: File to write; a relative path starts from the current directory. A name ending in .json is written as JSON, any other as binary protobuf. By default, the wish's title with .djinn in the Downloads folder.
The file to import, binary protobuf or JSON; a relative path starts from the current directory.

replace.description: Replace the wish if it is already here, with everything it holds. Without it, a wish already here is refused.

note.description: What to know, when there is something: an active wish imported paused, three being active here.

projects.description: How each of its projects was found on this machine.

paused.description: Make it paused: it waits, out of the three active wishes.

projectIds.description: A project the wish works on; repeat for each one.

title.description: What you wish, in a sentence.

to.description: Its new rank, from 1 for the first; beyond the last, it goes last.

file.description: File to write; a relative path starts from the current directory. By default, the wish's title with .html in the Downloads folder.

provider.description: Kind of agent for a new lead, when the wish has none to resume: claude (the default), codex or antigravity.

attached.description: The lead was already running: the window attached to it, nothing was started.

command.description: The command line the terminal runs, program first.

note.description: What to know, when there is something: no session to resume, a terminal that runs something else.

terminal.description: Name of the lead's terminal in the window.

directory.description: Folder the session runs in. By default, the folder of the wish's first project.

provider.description: Kind of agent: claude (the default) or codex.

sessionId.description: Identifier of the lead's session, as the agent names it.

file.description: The page, kept up to date: always the same file for a wish.

plan.v1.WishState.description: WishState is where a wish stands. A djinn grants three wishes at a time, never more: three are active at most.

bearer.description: The token of an http address in server.addr. The Unix socket needs none.

info.description:
The public methods of Djinn, generated from the protos in api/ (go tool task gen). They are the commands of the djinn command line and the tools of djinn mcp.

Each method is a POST of the [Connect protocol](https://connectrpc.com/docs/protocol): `Content-Type: application/json`, the request in protobuf JSON as the body. djinn up writes its address in `server.addr` of the data directory: on macOS and Linux a Unix socket, `curl --unix-socket <data>/djinn.sock http://localhost/plan.v1.ProjectService/List -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'`; on Windows or with `djinn up --browser`, `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/?token=…`, whose token goes in an `Authorization: Bearer` header.

The streaming methods use Connect's streaming protocol and are not described here: `/machine.v1.GateService/Hold`, `/plan.v1.TaskService/Watch`, `/plan.v1.WishService/Watch`.
info.title: Djinn

post.description: List what the commands of the projects cost, the most run first.
List the gates held or waited for.
Show the machine: its cores and memory, the live load and pressure, and the most workers Djinn runs at once.
Delete a block.
List the blocks of a wish, in order.
Add a block to a wish, or change one: given its id, the fields set replace those of the block.
List the marks of a wish, the latest last.
Mark a question, a decision or a block: read, or approved as it is. Approving an open question answers it with the option its recommendation names, as djinn question answer does.
Add a folder as a project. It need not be a Git repository.
List the projects.
Answer a question, which turns it into a decision.
Ask the developer a question. Offer up to four options to answer by letter, or none for a yes/no question.
Ask to investigate an open question before deciding: it waits for the lead, who finds out more and revises it.
List questions, the most recent last.
Revise an open question after investigating: its context, options or recommendation. The former ones stay in its rounds, and the question waits for the developer again.
List the skills of the projects: their own, and those they summon, with the ones whose source is missing.
Summon a skill of one project into another: djinn skill summon app/babysit-mr --into infra. Its workers get it from their next launch on; nothing is written in either project.
Unsummon a skill: the project's next workers no longer get it. The project stays as it was.
Remove the worktree of a finished task. Its branch stays.
Delete a task no worker of this Djinn ran (a plan item, a task imported from another Djinn): it goes with its events. A task a worker of this Djinn ran stays, as the record of that work.
Show a task.
List the tasks, the oldest first.
Pause a running worker without killing it: it holds still, keeps what it did, and frees its slot of the machine until it is resumed. Not possible on Windows yet.
Let a paused worker go on where it was.
Send a message to a running worker: an instruction added while it works. The message is an event of the task, and a "received" event follows once the worker says something after it.

Start a worker on a new task: in a Git project, in a new worktree on its own branch. A task that cannot start yet (a dependency not done, its write scope taken, no slot free, the machine under pressure) waits, and says why; djinn up starts it as soon as it can.
Stop a task's worker: asked to stop, then killed if it has not after a few seconds. A planned task that has not started is stopped at once.
Make a paused or granted wish active again, last by rank. Three wishes are active at most: pause or grant one first.

Allow the wish's workers a right in one of its projects, for every task to come: edit, or auto (edit in their agent's auto mode); none takes it back. It weighs over the project's configuration, for this wish only.

The brief of a wish: a short text to start an agent on it, written by Djinn from the store, no model. First what rarely changes (Djinn's rules, the rules of its projects), then where the wish stands (questions, decisions, tasks running and waiting, the latest blocks), so an agent reads the first part from its cache. No local path, no secret.

Export a wish to a file, to open it on another machine: its plan, questions, decisions, blocks and journal. Never code, which travels through Git, never a secret, never a local path: projects are named by their name and remote.
Grant a wish: you say it is done. Djinn never grants a wish itself; it proposes it once the wish is ready (every task finished, no question open), and you may grant it before.
Import a wish from a file written by export. Each project is found on this machine by its remote, then by its name; one not found is added without a folder, for djinn project add <folder> to attach.
List the wishes: the active ones by rank, the first has priority; then the paused ones and the granted ones, the most recent last.
Make a wish.
Move an active wish to another rank: --to 1 gives it priority over the others.
Pause a wish: it keeps everything, and leaves its place among the three active wishes to another one.

Render the wish's page to a file: one HTML page standing alone, with its open questions first, then what waits for you, its tasks, its decisions, its blocks and its journal. Djinn writes it, no model does. No secret, no local path.

Take a wish back where it stopped: show it in the window, and resume its lead in the lead's terminal, or attach to it if it runs. Without a lead session, a new lead starts in the wish's first project from the wish's brief (djinn wish brief), and claude's session is recorded as the wish's lead. Starts djinn if it is not running.
Record the lead of a wish: the agent session that drives it, for djinn wish resume to take it back. Starts djinn if it is not running.

Render the wish's page in Djinn's data folder, print where, and keep it up to date while djinn up runs: every change of the wish renders it again, at most once a second. Publishing it stays yours: share the file, or republish it where you put it last time. Delete the file to stop.

servers.description: The address in server.addr: the Unix socket, or the loopback port.

tags.description: Blocks: the free content of a wish, beside its tasks and questions.
tags.name: BlockService

tags.description: CommandService keeps what the commands of each project cost. Djinn measures each command a worker runs through djinn gate run: its CPU time, its peak memory and its duration, so that it learns what a project's usual commands cost.
tags.name: CommandService

tags.description: GateService grants the gates: shared resources, such as code generation (codegen), the local stack (stack), an end-to-end run (e2e) or a paid model run (paid), each held by one holder at a time, and granted only while the machine is not under pressure. To run a command under a gate: djinn gate run <name> -- <command>.
tags.name: GateService

tags.description: MachineService says what the machine has, how loaded it is, and how many workers Djinn runs on it.
tags.name: MachineService

tags.description: Marks: what the developer read or approved from the window, on questions, decisions and blocks, so that the lead acts on a click without a word.
tags.name: MarkService

tags.description: Questions agents ask, and the decisions taken.
tags.name: QuestionService

tags.description: Skills: what a project's agents know how to do, one folder each in the Agent Skills format (a SKILL.md, maybe scripts and references), in .agents/skills or .claude/skills. A project summons a skill of another project to use it without copying it: it follows its source.
tags.name: SkillService

tags.description: Tasks: one worker each, an agent process in the task's own worktree.
tags.name: TaskService

tags.description: Wishes: what you ask Djinn for, across projects.
